item.title: Why I Built Scorekeeping by Rounds
item.description: The origin story of a trivia scorekeeping app, scorekeeping-by-rounds.
item.content:encoded:
It started because I had a cousin pass away, and so his parents, my aunt and uncle, decided to do organ donation, saving/assiting many lifes in the process. They got involved with Saint Louis Transplant of America, and during the yearly trivia game I inquired about how to change the organizers from using Excel. I found the format to be a very poor user experience from the audience's perspective.

The lady in charge said it would have to be some free tool, and at the time I was working a job that had 10% learning time, developing software for them. The tech stack there used Angular, so I decided to practice my skills and make a website. I completed this project, and adoption turned out harder than I thought.

To fundraise for his scholarship, my aunt and uncle held a disc golf tournament in his honor. They did that for several years, then migrated to a local trivia night they host every year. My niece has used this as scorekeeper every year, providing a great experience. She can edit scores on one monitor and have the scores display on the monitor projected to the audience.
